hook: A speedometer shows 64 miles per hour at this very instant. But a speed is distance divided by time, and in an instant no time passes and no distance is covered. Zero divided by zero is not a number. So what does the speedometer mean? Answering that question is where calculus begins.

prereq.q: What is the slope of the line through $(1, 4)$ and $(3, 10)$?

figure.caption: A falling stone, $s(t) = 16t^2$: the average speed from $t = 1$ over shorter and shorter intervals closes in on 32 feet per second.

chain.cause: Over an interval [a, b], divide the change in a quantity by the change in time
chain.effect: the average rate of change $\frac{f(b) - f(a)}{b - a}$, the slope of the line through two points of the graph

chain.cause: At a single instant the interval has length 0
chain.effect: the quotient becomes zero divided by zero, which has no value

chain.cause: Shrink the interval around the instant instead
chain.effect: the average rates close in on one number

chain.cause: That number is what the average rates approach
chain.effect: it is the instantaneous rate of change: the speed the speedometer shows

ideas: The average rate of change of $f$ over $[a, b]$ is $\frac{f(b) - f(a)}{b - a}$: the slope of the line through $(a, f(a))$ and $(b, f(b))$. Its units are output units per input unit.
A rate of change at one instant cannot be computed as a quotient, because the interval would have length 0.
The instantaneous rate of change at $t = a$ is the number the average rates over shorter and shorter intervals around $a$ close in on.
From a table, estimate the rate at an instant with the shortest interval that contains it; from both sides, average the two closest rates.
A negative rate means the quantity is decreasing; its size tells how fast.

misconception.wrong: The average rate over $[0, 5]$ tells how fast the quantity is changing at $t = 5$.
misconception.right: An average rate describes a whole interval. The rate at one instant can be very different; estimate it from the shortest interval around that instant, and interpret averages with the words "on average over the interval".

summary: An average rate of change, $\frac{f(b) - f(a)}{b - a}$, is a slope over an interval, with units of output per input. A rate at one instant cannot be a quotient, since nothing changes in zero time; instead, the averages over shrinking intervals close in on one number, the instantaneous rate of change. The next topic gives that closing in a name and a notation.
